US-119-HR10948.title: Hire Our Heroes Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10948.description: To amend title 38, United States Code, to extend the veterans' employment emphasis under Federal contracts to military spouses, to increase thresholds relating to the applicability of such emphases, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10948.aiSummary: The bill would expand federal hiring and advancement rules for veterans to include military spouses. It would apply these rules to larger federal contractors, and raise the contract amount threshold from $100,000 to $5,000,000. It would also require certain contractors, colleges, and research groups to report hiring numbers and related efforts, and to post that information on a public website.

US-119-HR10926.title: Election Worker and Polling Place Protection Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10926.description: To protect election workers and polling places.
US-119-HR10926.aiSummary: The bill would add new penalties for using force, threats, or violence to interfere with voting, poll watchers, election officials, and people helping run elections. It would also make it a crime to damage or threaten to damage polling places, tabulation centers, or other election equipment. Penalties could include fines up to $2,500 or up to 6 months in jail, and higher penalties up to $5,000 or 1 year if someone is injured or a dangerous weapon, explosive, or fire is used. The Justice Department could bring a federal case only in certain situations, such as when a state lacks jurisdiction or asks the federal government to step in.

US-119-HCONRES125.title: Expressing support for the designation of the week of November 9 through November 15, 2026, as "National Caregiving Youth Week" to raise awareness and encourage national recognition of children and adolescents under 18 years of age who serve as a primary or secondary caregiver for family or household members.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
Submitted in House

US-119-HCONRES125.aiSummary: This resolution would support designating November 9 through November 15, 2026, as National Caregiving Youth Week. It would recognize children under 18 who help care for family or household members and encourage more awareness of their needs. It would also urge schools, health workers, and researchers to help identify these youth and connect them with support.

US-119-HR10904.title: American Cost of Living Defense Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10904.description: To direct the Federal Trade Commission to convene an interagency working group to track and report on market concentration and monopoly activity with respect to certain sectors of the economy, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10904.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Federal Trade Commission to lead a group of federal agencies to track and report on market concentration and monopoly activity in certain parts of the economy. It would require public reports on things like top firms' market share, supply chain bottlenecks, and possible pricing coordination, with graphs and charts for the public. The sectors covered could include basic goods and services such as food, fuel, rent, drugs, and phone service.

US-119-HR10849.title: Small Business and Defense Industrial Base Support Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10849.description: To amend chapter 388 of title 10, United States Code, to clarify to the purpose of and adjust the limits on assistance under the procurement technical assistance cooperative agreement program.
US-119-HR10849.aiSummary: The bill would change a Defense Department program that helps small businesses with procurement, which means getting goods and services for the government. It would say the help is for confidential procurement assistance and raise some funding limits from $1.5 million to $2 million and from $750,000 to $1 million. It would also let the Secretary change those dollar limits in some cases and notify Congress within 30 days.

US-119-HR10827.title: Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Financial Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10827.description: To require the Secretary of State to submit a report identifying senior Syrian officials alleged to have facilitated certain human rights abuses, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10827.aiSummary: The bill would require the Secretary of State, with the Director of National Intelligence, to send Congress a report naming senior Syrian officials and related people who are credibly alleged to have helped with serious human rights abuses against religious and ethnic minorities. It would also ask for a finding on whether targeted penalties, like blocking property or visa limits, should be used under existing U.S. law. The bill says the United States supports accountability for abuses in Syria and the protection of minority communities.

US-119-HR10805.title: Don’t Block LGBTQ Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10805.description: To amend the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit schools and public libraries that receive universal service support from blocking internet access to lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer resources, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10805.aiSummary: The bill would change federal communications law so elementary schools, secondary schools, and public libraries that get universal service support could not block internet access to LGBTQ resources if they want to keep discounted service rates. It defines LGBTQ resources as information about topics like homosexuality, bisexuality, transgender identity, gender identity, and sexual orientation. The bill was introduced in the House and referred to the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

US-119-HR10728.title: Maternity Care for Rural Communities Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10728.description: To provide that certain limits on State-directed payments under the Medicaid program not apply to certain maternity, labor, and delivery services.
US-119-HR10728.aiSummary: The bill would change Medicaid rules so some limits on state-directed payments would not apply to certain maternity, labor, and delivery services. It would affect rural hospitals, Indian Health Service or Tribal hospitals, and hospitals where at least half of births are qualifying births. actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.

US-119-S5589.description: A bill to prohibit United States foreign assistance to the Palestinian Authority and other Palestinian governing entities in the West Bank and Gaza unless certain conditions are met, and for other purposes.

US-119-HR10409.title: Lethal Means Safety Training Act

US-119-HR10409.description: To direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to update the Lethal Means Safety and Suicide Prevention training course of the Department of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes.

US-119-HR4646.title: Whistleblower Protection Act of 2025
US-119-HR4646.summary:
Whistleblower Protection Act of 2025

This bill expands existing whistleblower protections for employees of federal contractors or grant recipients to apply to all contracts and grants funded by the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) regardless of the date of execution.

Current law protects employees of federal contractors or grant recipients from a reprisal (i.e., discharge, demotion, or discrimination) for disclosing evidence to Congress or another appropriate official of certain misconduct involving federal contracts, grants, or funds. This provision currently applies only to contracts and grants signed or modified after the law took effect in 2013. The bill expands these protections to apply to HUD contracts and grants signed before the law was enacted.

US-119-HR9937.title: No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act
US-119-HR9937.summary:
No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act

This bill modifies the drug quantity thresholds that trigger a mandatory minimum prison term for a defendant who manufactures, distributes, imports, exports, or possesses with intent to distribute fentanyl.

Specifically, the bill reduces from 400 to 20 grams the fentanyl quantity and from 100 to 5 grams the fentanyl analogue quantity that trigger a mandatory minimum prison term for high-level first-time or repeat offenders. It also reduces from 40 to 2 grams the fentanyl quantity and from 10 to 0.5 grams the fentanyl analogue quantity that trigger a mandatory minimum prison term for low-level first-time or repeat offenders.

Additionally, the bill directs the U.S. Postal Service to increase the availability of chemical screening devices and dedicate the appropriate number of personnel to interdict fentanyl and other substances that are unlawfully imported into the United States.
US-119-HR9937.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-07-23)

US-119-HR9937.aiSummary: The bill would lower the fentanyl amounts that can trigger a required prison term for people who make, sell, import, export, or have fentanyl with the intent to sell it. It would also lower the amounts for fentanyl-like drugs, called fentanyl analogues. The U.S. Postal Service would be told to make more chemical screening devices available and assign enough staff to help stop fentanyl and other illegal imports.

US-119-HR9915.title: Stealth Bot Prohibition Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9915.description: To prohibit stealth bots, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9915.aiSummary: The bill would ban “stealth bots,” meaning software that accesses websites or online services without clearly saying who it is or why it is there. It would also bar bots from hiding that they are bots when used with generative AI tools, and it would let the Federal Trade Commission and state officials take civil action. Violations could bring civil penalties of up to $53,000 per violation, and the rule would take effect 180 days after enactment.

US-119-HR9816.title: MOMMIES Act
US-119-HR9816.summary:
Maximizing Outcomes for Moms through Medicaid Improvement and Enhancement of Services Act or the MOMMIES Act

This bill establishes a series of programs and requirements under Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) relating to maternal health.

For example, the bill expands eligibility for coverage under Medicaid and CHIP from 60 days to one year after the last day of pregnancy and requires such coverage to include oral health services.

The bill also establishes a demonstration program in which states receive grants to implement or expand models for maternity care homes that provide services to Medicaid or CHIP beneficiaries.

The Government Accountability Office must report on (1) gaps in coverage under Medicaid and CHIP for pregnant and postpartum women, and (2) the use of telehealth by state Medicaid programs to increase access to maternity care.
US-119-HR9816.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-07-21)

US-119-HR9816.aiSummary: The bill would change Medicaid and CHIP rules for maternal health. It would extend coverage for some mothers from 60 days to one year after pregnancy ends, and that coverage would include dental care. It would also create state grants for maternity care homes and require a federal report on coverage gaps and telehealth use in state Medicaid programs.

US-119-S4632.title: Prevent Government Shutdowns Act of 2026
US-119-S4632.summary:
Prevent Government Shutdowns Act of 2026

This bill provides continuing appropriations to prevent a government shutdown if the appropriations bills for a fiscal year have not been enacted before the fiscal year begins and continuing appropriations are not in effect.

Specifically, the bill provides appropriations at the rate of operations that was provided for the prior fiscal year to continue programs, projects, and activities that were funded in the preceding fiscal year.

The bill also limits official travel, congressional recesses or adjournments, and the consideration of legislation that is unrelated to appropriations after the beginning of a fiscal year if the appropriations process has not been completed.

US-119-HR8705.title: CHARLIE Act
US-119-HR8705.summary:
Civics and History Advancement to Restore Learning, Integrity, and Education Act or the CHARLIE Act

This bill prohibits the use of federal funding made available for the American History and Civics Education program to fund discriminatory equity ideology or gender ideology, as defined in certain executive orders. Further, in awarding grants under this program, the Department of Education may not give priority to an eligible entity on the basis of race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or immigration status.

The bill defines discriminatory equity ideology in accordance with Executive Order 14190 , which was published on January 29, 2025. This definition refers to ideology that treats individuals as members of preferred or disfavored groups rather than as individuals, including listed ideologies (e.g., an ideology that members of one race, color, sex, or national origin are morally or inherently superior to members of another race, color, sex, or national origin, or that an individual is inherently racist, sexist, or oppressive by virtue of the individual's race, color, sex, or national origin).

The bill defines gender ideology in accordance with Executive Order 14168 , which was published on January 20, 2025. This definition refers to an ideology that replaces categories of biological sex with gender identity.
